item.title: Associate Director or Director of Career Development, School of Architecture
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 10/6/2026.

Note: The final title and salary will be determined based on qualifications and experience. No visa sponsorship. Hybrid in Charlottesville, VA (3 days on-grounds/week after onboarding). A master's degree is required. Cover letter and resume required. Apply via UVA jobs portal, requisition R0087535. Application review begins after October 5, 2026.

The University of Virginia School of Architecture seeks a collaborative and innovative Associate Director or Director of Career Development to lead career services for undergraduate and graduate students across design disciplines. This role oversees career advising, professional development programming, and employer engagement initiatives, and builds relationships with alumni, employers, and corporate partners to expand career opportunities. Reporting to the Associate Dean of Student Affairs. Salary: $70,000-$75,000 (Associate Director) or $75,000-$85,000 (Director).

Key responsibilities include (Student Advising and Program Development): providing career advising on internship and job search strategies, resumes, portfolios, digital profiles, interviewing, salary negotiation, and career planning; leading the development, implementation, and assessment of signature career education and employer engagement initiatives including Career Week, career fairs, portfolio reviews, networking events, and industry site visits; managing and expanding experiential learning opportunities including externships, professional immersion experiences, and firm treks; and partnering with student organizations, faculty, and staff to support student-led professional development. (External Partners and Relations): pursuing, cultivating, and strengthening relationships with employers to source internship and job opportunities; collaborating with the Advancement Team and UVA's University Career Center; and developing and sustaining an alumni engagement strategy. (Fiscal Management): at the Director level, developing and managing the annual operating budget and building corporate sponsorships; and advising Associate Deans on financial sustainability of Career Development. (Assessment): leading the collection, analysis, and reporting of First Destination Survey and other career outcomes data; and establishing, monitoring, and reporting key performance indicators.

Qualifications: a master's degree; Associate Director: 2+ years of experience in career services, higher education administration, student affairs, employer relations, workforce development, or recruiting; Director: 5+ years; demonstrated success in career advising and building partnerships with employers and alumni; and experience utilizing career technologies to assess outcomes. No visa sponsorship.

Compensation and logistics: salary $70,000-$75,000 (Associate Director) or $75,000-$85,000 (Director), commensurate with education and experience. Comprehensive UVA benefits. Hybrid in Charlottesville, VA (3 days on-grounds/week). Review begins after October 5, 2026.

item.title: Energy Analyst
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date — candidates are strongly encouraged to apply by October 5, 2026. The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 10/6/2026.

The Virginia State Corporation Commission's Division of Public Utility Regulation (PUR) seeks an Energy Analyst for a rewarding public service career. PUR provides support to the Commission in its regulation of Virginia's investor-owned electric, natural gas, water, and sewer utilities; member-owned electric cooperatives; and the telecommunications industry. The position offers a hybrid work schedule (generally 3 days telework, 2 days in office), continuing education, professional development opportunities, and career growth in Richmond, VA. Salary $54,808-$70,000.

Key responsibilities include: investigating electric and gas utility proposals for rate increases, certificates of public convenience and necessity, integrated resource plans, demand side management programs, and renewable portfolio standard plans; conducting jurisdictional and class cost of service studies of utility rate proposals; designing rates for each rate class to recover the revenue requirement; performing statistical analysis of utility proposals; monitoring Organization of PJM States Inc., PJM Interconnection, LLC, and Federal Energy Regulatory Commission related conferences, meetings, and presentations; documenting findings of investigations in pre-filed written testimony and reports; and defending findings as an expert witness at evidentiary hearings.

Qualifications: without related professional experience, the minimum requirement is a bachelor's degree in accounting, business, economics, finance, mathematics, public administration, statistics, or a related field; professional experience with financial or economic analysis, linear regressions, statistical analysis, and/or cost-benefit analysis preferred; experience or exposure to utility cost of service studies and/or knowledge of PJM energy and capacity markets a plus; ability to conduct investigations to determine compliance with existing statutes, rules, and regulations; exceptional research skills with highly detailed analysis and strong reading comprehension; and ability to convey technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Compensation and logistics: salary $54,808-$70,000. Comprehensive Virginia state benefits. Hybrid in Richmond, VA (generally 3 days telework, 2 days in office). Strongly encouraged to apply by October 5, 2026. Apply via the SCC Career Center at careercenter.scc.virginia.gov (external candidates).

item.title: Government Relations Coordinator
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 10/6/2026.

Note: Staff are required to work in the office a minimum of 3 days per week (Monday-Wednesday) and must live in MD, DC, or VA. Overnight and out-of-state travel required, including to twice-yearly conferences. Resume and cover letter required.

340B Health is a national nonprofit health care trade association that assists safety-net hospitals in providing services to more patients with low incomes and those living in rural areas. The Government Relations Coordinator will support efforts to shape the strategies and tactics to effectively represent the organization on Capitol Hill, with the administration, and throughout the 340B provider community. The GR Coordinator plays an integral role in government relations activities and collaborates with 340B Health member hospitals to engage in advocacy. Washington, DC. Salary $56,000-$75,000.

Key responsibilities include: assisting the Director of Grassroots in executing two lobby day events per year for member hospitals including event logistics, program and materials preparation, participant recruitment, and post-event analysis and follow-up; maintaining GR team calendars and coordinating meeting invitations; arranging and supporting meetings and calls with members, outside consultants, and other stakeholders; assisting the Director of Grassroots in working with member hospitals to develop and share with policymakers the impact 340B has on their hospitals and patients; monitoring and informing staff of 340B activity on Capitol Hill including legislation, hearings, and other congressional activity; assisting in administering the Champions Recognition Program; maintaining the government relations database; attending and assisting with bi-annual conferences; and assisting with developing and editing written materials such as talking points, policy summaries, PowerPoint presentations for lobby days, and government relations webinars.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree required; professional experience in a legislative setting or in government relations a plus; strong writing and communication skills; knowledge of Congress and the legislative process preferred; strong organizational and time management skills; and experience using Microsoft Office suite. Must live in MD, DC, or VA.

Compensation and logistics: salary $56,000-$75,000 based on experience. Exceptional benefits package including health, dental, life insurance, disability insurance, paid time off, and retirement plan matching. Hybrid in Washington, DC (M-W in office required). Overnight and out-of-state travel required for twice-yearly conferences. Resume and cover letter required.

item.title: Research Analyst – Navy Support
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 10/6/2026.

Note: Must be a U.S. citizen and able to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance. This is an early-career opportunity. Salary $95,000-$115,000.

RPI Group is seeking a curious, driven Research Analyst to support a dynamic Navy customer in Washington, DC. You'll join a small, growing, fast-moving team that works closely with senior leaders across the Navy's science and technology (S&T) community. This is an outstanding opportunity for recent graduates who want to make an impact early in their career.

Key responsibilities include: diving into diverse sources -- academic research, technical reports, policies, journals, and open-source materials -- to extract insights and connect dots across complex topics; producing clear and compelling quantitative and qualitative analyses; developing studies, papers, and presentations that translate technical research into options for decision-makers; framing key research questions, conducting analysis, and briefing findings to Navy leadership; coordinating technical analysis across scientists, engineers, analysts, and policymakers; and leading or participating in small project teams.

Qualifications: a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution with strong academic performance in fields such as national security studies, policy, engineering, natural sciences, social sciences, or management; excellent research, analytical, and communication skills (written and verbal); U.S. citizenship required; ability to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance; and proficiency with Microsoft Office. Master's degree in a relevant field preferred; experience using research databases, data-analytics tools, knowledge-management platforms, or AI technologies preferred.

Compensation and logistics: salary $95,000-$115,000 annually. Washington, DC. U.S. citizenship required. Secret security clearance required (ability to obtain). Early-career opportunity.

item.title: Policy Analyst
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 10/6/2026.

Note: This position is 100% remote. A master's degree in a relevant discipline is required, plus 1 year of related work experience (internships and research assistant roles requiring analysis, writing, or research qualify). Salary $65,000-$77,000.

The UMass Chan Medical School Department of Health Policy Strategy & Analytics seeks a Policy Analyst responsible for supporting policy analysis, writing, and research activities. The Policy Analyst identifies, obtains, organizes, and analyzes quantitative and qualitative data, reviews academic and professional literature, and gathers information from multiple sources on the costs, utilization, quality, and access to health care and human services. 100% remote. Salary $65,000-$77,000.

Key responsibilities include: performing policy and data analyses of health care and human services topics and issues, combining and synthesizing data and information from multiple sources; preparing written summaries and reports of policy and data analyses and providing input to written reports and other materials in easily understood formats for both internal and external distribution; obtaining data and information from a wide variety of sources including federal agencies, state agencies, insurers, health care providers, academic journals, and consulting project partners; assessing the quality of data obtained by analyzing for missing data and/or inconsistencies; organizing data by constructing databases and spreadsheets; and assisting in identifying sources of data and information relevant to specific analytic projects.

Qualifications: a master's degree in a relevant discipline (public policy, law, public health, health economics, public or business administration with a concentration in health care, or equivalent) required; one year of related work experience required (internships or research assistant roles requiring analysis, writing, or research qualify); excellent quantitative and qualitative policy research and analytical skills; excellent analytical and writing skills; and ability to work independently and take initiative on assignments. Knowledge of the Massachusetts health care system and federal/state legislative and regulatory processes preferred.

Compensation and logistics: salary $65,000-$77,000. Comprehensive UMass Chan benefits including paid time off, medical, dental, and vision coverage, and participation in a 401(a)-retirement plan with optional 403(b) plan. 100% remote. Master's degree + 1 year experience required.

item.title: Associate Policy Analyst, Global Program
item.description:
Application deadline: September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET. Apply by submitting a cover letter, resume, and a 1,000-word writing sample on an immigration policy of your choosing to hr@migrationpolicy.org. Label each file with your last name. Use 'Associate Policy Analyst - Global Program' as the subject line and include how you heard about the position. AI tools may be used in the writing sample but must be disclosed. No phone calls or emails to MPI staff. Only candidates being considered will be contacted.

The Migration Policy Institute (MPI) is an independent, nonpartisan, evidence-informed think tank focused on the movement of people worldwide. The Global Program acts as a policy laboratory for innovative, evidence-based, and politically feasible solutions to migration policy challenges, with an established portfolio of projects in Latin America, East Africa, and Europe, and emerging work in South/Southeast Asia, the Middle East and North Africa, and Australia. The Associate Policy Analyst will support the team with rigorous empirical research and comparative analysis on a range of migration policy topics. This position offers direct exposure to MPI's behind-the-scenes policy advising and convening. The role is based in Washington, DC; remote work worldwide will be considered for the right candidate. Master's degree + 3-5 years required. Salary $62,000-$67,000 (U.S.-based).

Key responsibilities include: delivering in-depth policy analysis with clear interpretations and actionable recommendations, and helping shape the methodology behind new research projects; drafting and editing background notes, analytical reports, policy briefs, and other research materials with minimal supervision and under tight deadlines; contributing to and co-authoring MPI publications and short-form work, with opportunities to single- or lead-author policy briefs as experience grows; assisting senior staff in fundraising and grant management duties including contributing to grant proposals and reports; supporting the organization of high-level roundtables and private meetings including developing agendas and concept notes, liaising with participants, and briefing speakers; and, in time, engaging with the news media.

Qualifications: a master's degree with 3-5 years of direct experience, or equivalent combination; strong research and analytical skills with the ability to collect and make sense of large volumes of data from primary and secondary sources; knowledge of international migration trends and policies with specific expertise in one or more countries outside the United States preferred (particularly in Africa, Latin America, or Europe); sharp writing and oral communication skills; and high motivation with the ability to juggle multiple assignments in a fast-paced environment. Experience conducting original quantitative analysis using statistical programming software is a plus.

Compensation and logistics: salary $62,000-$67,000 (U.S.-based; remote worldwide compensation reviewed based on candidate's location and local regulations). Generous MPI benefits package. Washington, DC (remote worldwide considered). Deadline: September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET.

item.title: Sr. Policy Analyst
item.description:
Application review begins October 11, 2026 and will continue on a rolling basis thereafter.

Voices for Virginia's Children is hiring a Sr. Policy Analyst to drive statewide, systems-level change with a focus on Early Childhood Care & Education and Maternal Health policy. The Sr. Policy Analyst will analyze policy and data, develop and advance legislative and administrative solutions, build relationships with policymakers and partners, and help translate complex policy issues into actionable strategies for change. This role requires a minimum of 3 years of experience in state-level policy advocacy. The position is hybrid in Richmond, VA (Wednesdays in-office required; additional in-person days required during the Virginia General Assembly session). Salary $68,000-$74,000.

Key responsibilities include (Policy Advocacy and Leadership): leading Voices' policy work in early childhood care and education and maternal health; working collaboratively with policy and engagement staff to create and advance a multi-disciplinary policy agenda for infants, young children, and families; monitoring legislative and administrative developments; analyzing policy and research; identifying opportunities for systems change; developing evidence-based policy recommendations; providing policy analysis support to internal and external partners; and having primary responsibility for advancing these issue areas during Virginia's General Assembly session. (Community Relationship Building): leading and participating in various coalitions within the focus area; serving as the main Voices liaison for partner organizations; providing support and technical assistance to partner coalitions and state workgroups; and working in partnership with the Director of Engagement and Virginia's Youth in Action (VAYA) members to ensure that youth voice and lived expertise are centered in policy recommendations. (Strategic Communications): working with the Communications Manager on developing and executing communications including policy briefs, one-pagers, blogs, and other advocacy materials; and conducting and participating in trainings and presentations. (Racial Equity): promoting racial equity across all dimensions of work, ensuring that policies put forward are assessed for their impact on all races.

Qualifications: strong verbal and written communication skills; a minimum of 3 years of experience working in state-level policy advocacy with knowledge of the Virginia state legislative process and evidence-based policymaking; ability to build relationships with legislators, community members, partner organizations, and other stakeholders; ability to effectively analyze data and research to identify trends and inform policymaking; and strong commitment to social, economic, and racial justice with active centering of equity and inclusion. Candidates should bring substantive knowledge in at least one of early childhood care and education or maternal health and demonstrate the ability to quickly develop expertise across both areas.

Compensation and logistics: salary $68,000-$74,000 (to preserve opportunity for salary growth, Voices typically does not hire above the mid-range). Benefits include fully covered health, dental, and vision employee premiums, health and dependent care FSAs, 30 days of PTO and 12 paid holidays, paid parental leave, a retirement plan with 3% employer contribution (no required employee match), professional development stipend, and monthly remote work stipend. Hybrid in Richmond, VA (Wednesdays in-office required; additional in-person during GA session). Application review begins October 11, 2026.

item.title: Youth Development Specialist – El Salvador
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 9/29/2026.

Note: Peace Corps Volunteers receive a living stipend, not a salary. This is a two-year volunteer commitment requiring U.S. citizenship. Volunteers live and work in host communities, receiving a stipend and other support including housing, medical care, and a readjustment allowance upon completion of service.

The Peace Corps is seeking U.S. citizens to serve as Youth Development Specialists in El Salvador. Youth make up more than a quarter of El Salvador's population, yet many young people face social and economic challenges including economic hardship, low school completion rates, limited life skills development opportunities, and barriers to civic engagement. Only half of youth complete lower secondary school and even fewer complete upper secondary school. As a Youth Development Specialist, you will collaborate with school staff to equip youth with essential life skills such as communication, empathy, creative problem-solving, and goal setting, working alongside community leaders to create supportive environments that encourage youth participation in community projects and civic engagement.

Key responsibilities include: collaborating with school staff to teach essential life skills to youth; working alongside community leaders to create supportive environments for youth participation; contributing to community projects and civic engagement initiatives; building relationships with host community members; and exchanging knowledge and helping transform lives for future generations.

Qualifications: U.S. citizenship required; bachelor's degree (typical requirement for Peace Corps service); demonstrated commitment to community development, education, or youth work. Visit the Peace Corps El Salvador project page for full details and application information.

Compensation and logistics: living stipend provided (not a salary); additional benefits include housing support, medical and dental care, language and cultural training, and a readjustment allowance upon completion of service. El Salvador. 2-year commitment. U.S. citizenship required.
